hero.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in U.S., financial stress cited
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie ranks as the 67th most stressed city in the United States according to a WalletHub study released this month. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

The report cited Port St. Lucie as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America. Jacksonville ranked as the most stressed city in Florida at number 37 nationally. In South Florida, Miami placed at number 50, with affordable housing ranking fourth worst in the country, while Fort Lauderdale came in at number 83.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. He noted that some stress is out of people's control due to issues with family, friends or employers, but where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are. Lupo emphasized the importance of considering how a certain city may impact your mental health when moving, not just your financial opportunities. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the United States. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area ranked as the least stressed city. The notably affluent area has average home prices of about $1.5 million. South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota followed as the next least stressed cities. Florida performed fairly well overall, with no cities in the top 35 most stressed.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher shot and killed; family member arrested in connection with death
cards.teaser: Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children. His family released a statement about his death, saying they are sad to report the loss of their dad to a senseless act of violence. The family asked people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online discussing any other details as this remains an active investigation.

Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as more than just an educator. "Mr. Barnes was really a pillar of the community to us. I didn't grow up with a dad; some of my friends didn't either. We really looked at him as a father figure," Coleman said. Coleman said Barnes made a lasting impression that endured well beyond the classroom. "He made an impact on us life-long. I'm 37 years old now and he was my teacher in 7th grade. So for us to have kept communication that long, well before social media even came around, says a lot about his character," Coleman said. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Two bodies found near Sebastian appear unconnected but remain suspicious, Indian River County sheriff says
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Thursday that two bodies discovered this week near Sebastian appear unconnected but both cases remain under investigation as suspicious deaths. Sheriff Eric Flowers held a news conference Thursday morning to address the findings after autopsies were completed on both bodies.

The first body was found Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. The deceased was identified as James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident who had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian. Thompson was last seen Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. Flowers said Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues and had made a purchase of methamphetamine on July 3 before going into a manic state. The sheriff said Thompson had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County many times. According to Flowers, there was only a minor contusion on Thompson's eyebrow with no signs of violence.

The second body was found Wednesday shortly after 4 p.m. in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian and across the street from Monday's location. The heavily decomposed body was that of a 65-year-old man with a temporary address at his brother's home in Sebastian. The man had been out of jail on pretrial release after being arrested by Plantation police on a charge of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon in Broward County. Flowers said Plantation police had just obtained or was in the process of obtaining a warrant for him for absconding on his pretrial release. The man had a serious history of seizures and his brother had taken him to a hospital on Sunday. The man walked away from the hospital against medical advice around 7:30 a.m. Sunday while still wearing hospital socks, with his brother last seeing him walking north. Flowers quoted the man as saying he was not going back to the hospital.

Flowers said autopsies on both bodies showed no stab wounds or signs of violence, and nothing at this point connects the two cases. The sheriff's office is waiting on toxicology results to determine the causes of death. Flowers said the deaths could be the result of bad fentanyl or methamphetamine circulating in the area and urged drug users to seek treatment. He said the office will investigate who may have sold drugs to the men if toxicology reveals drug-related issues. Anyone with information in either case is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Neighbors push back on proposed 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but neighbors say it will transform the area's rural character.
cards.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but not without pushback from neighbors who say it will transform the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August. The proposed development is 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres.

Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. She said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. "We will be surrounded. I think that there's plenty of other places for them to build."

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. She said the overlay district is trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities, and considers compatibility with the county's need for infrastructure, quality of life, jobs and connectivity to the interstate and roadway system. Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. She said the design incorporates a lot of open space while keeping a native buffer along Indrio Road.

Lewis said she's worried this development will change the rural landscape in St. Lucie County. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do. We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like," Lewis said. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Park Vista Football Team Targets State Playoffs After Strong 2025 Finish
cards.teaser: Park Vista Community High School's Cobras are building on momentum from winning four of their last five games in 2025 as they aim for the state playoffs this season.
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building momentum heading into the 2026 season after a strong finish to last year's campaign. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025 but turned things around in the second half of the season, winning four of their last five games. Now the team is looking to carry that success through an entire season as they set their sights on reaching the state playoffs.

Senior Harris Bender reflected on how the team felt during their late-season surge and what it means for the upcoming year. "Felt good throughout the second half of that season," Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing." The Cobras' ultimate goal extends beyond just making the playoffs. The program is aiming for a state title, something Park Vista has not accomplished since 2017.

Head coach Donald Hanna emphasized the importance of staying focused on the immediate challenges ahead rather than looking too far down the road. "We got to take it one game at a time," Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." His approach reflects a measured mindset designed to keep the team grounded as they pursue their championship aspirations. The coach's philosophy centers on consistent weekly execution as the path to postseason success.

Senior Erik Lee acknowledged that while the roster has the talent necessary to achieve their goals, success will require dedication and effort from everyone involved. "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done," Lee said. "But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well." Senior Justice Jones expressed even stronger confidence in the team's ability to reach its objectives. "It's going to feel amazing, because I already know it's gonna happen, definitely," Jones said. Park Vista will open its 2026 season with a road game against Atlantic in August, providing an early test for a program eager to prove its late 2025 resurgence was the beginning of something bigger.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Manager Releases Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget
cards.teaser:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The propo
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The proposed budget represents a 12.12% increase from the current fiscal year, which the city says is driven by inflation and capital projects. The general fund budget is proposed at about $230.6 million, an 8.48% increase, or roughly $18 million more than FY 2025-26.

The city's taxable value is also expected to rise. According to the budget brief, Port St. Lucie's estimated certified taxable value increased 5.45%, from $25.5 billion in FY 2025-26 to $26.9 billion in FY 2026-27, due to growth and property appreciation.

Under the proposal, the operating millage rate would remain at 4.6607 per $1,000 of taxable value. The total proposed millage rate would remain 4.9750, including the voter-approved Crosstown Parkway debt service millage of 0.3143.

Residents could see some fee changes. The stormwater fee would increase by $6, bringing the residential rate to $195. The solid waste assessment would increase to $482.16 under the city's contract with its solid waste vendor, though qualified residential homeowners would receive a one-time credit of either $364 or $64. The city also proposes a 3.5% increase in the water rate, while the sewer rate would remain unchanged.

The proposed budget also includes long-term infrastructure planning. The city says capital improvement projects over the next five years are projected to cost about $1.069 billion. The largest portion is for utility system upgrades, listed at $672.7 million. Other planned spending includes $51.1 million for Walton & One, Torino & Tradition Regional Parks and O.L. Peacock Park, $34.8 million for facilities maintenance, $24.5 million for street resurfacing and $9.9 million for sidewalk projects.

The budget brief also notes that Port St. Lucie's long-term debt has declined from more than $1.042 billion in FY 2009-10 to a projected $765 million in FY 2026-27, a reduction of 26.58% over 16 years. The proposed budget includes a net increase of seven positions in the Utility Systems Fund, bringing the city to 1,550.25 full-time equivalent positions.

City Council will review the proposed budget during a workshop July 22-23 at the Community Center, located at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

The workshop will also be televised live on the city's website, Xfinity Channel 20 and Blue Stream Fiber Channel 20.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League Unveils Team Names and Logos
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League announced the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of the inaugural season starting August 1 in Springfield, Illinois.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The WPBL's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois, where games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium, and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that playing professional baseball is every little girl's dream and that there is freedom and peace in being with each other.

cards.headline: U.S. vs Belgium World Cup Match Draws Record 30 Million Viewers
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match became the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history with more than 30 million viewers tuning in.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. According to Fox, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi Leads Argentina to Dramatic 3-2 Comeback Win Over Egypt
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 2-0 deficit in the final 11 minutes to defeat Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday, with Lionel Messi scoring his eighth goal of the World Cup.
cards.body:
Argentina staged a dramatic comeback against Egypt on Tuesday, scoring three goals in the final 11 minutes to win 3-2 at the World Cup. Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez netted the winning goal in stoppage time to complete the rally after Cristian Romero started the comeback in the 79th minute. Egypt had taken a 2-0 lead on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico before Argentina's surge. The defending champions will face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri.

Messi had earlier missed a penalty kick that was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir and also hit the post when the score was 1-0. The 39-year-old Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Fernandez said four years have passed since Qatar and the team wants to win it again. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni called it a phenomenal group of players. Egypt took the lead in the 15th minute when Ibrahim headed in Marwan Attia's cross.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova Defeats Coco Gauff to Reach Wimbledon Final
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's Wimbledon run with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 victory Thursday that concluded with a dramatic tiebreaker on Centre Court.
cards.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, becoming the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. The ninth-ranked Muchova will compete in her second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova set to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who won the championship in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who won the championship in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The festival is organized by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc., which hosts the annual event in Vero Beach. The announcement was made Monday.

The seafood festival has been held annually in Vero Beach and is returning for its 18th year. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. produces the event.

The festival is scheduled to take place in November 2026 in Vero Beach.

Wallethub analyst Chip Lupo said where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are. "Cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. When moving, it's important to consider how a certain city may impact your mental health, not just your financial opportunities," Lupo said. Topping the list of most stressed cities in the U.S. were Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, topped the list of least stressed, followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Manager Releases Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget
cards.teaser:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The propo
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The proposed budget represents a 12.12% increase from the current fiscal year, which the city says is driven by inflation and capital projects. The general fund budget is proposed at about $230.6 million, an 8.48% increase, or roughly $18 million more than FY 2025-26.

The city's taxable value is also expected to rise. According to the budget brief, Port St. Lucie's estimated certified taxable value increased 5.45%, from $25.5 billion in FY 2025-26 to $26.9 billion in FY 2026-27, due to growth and property appreciation.

Under the proposal, the operating millage rate would remain at 4.6607 per $1,000 of taxable value. The total proposed millage rate would remain 4.9750, including the voter-approved Crosstown Parkway debt service millage of 0.3143.

Residents could see some fee changes. The stormwater fee would increase by $6, bringing the residential rate to $195. The solid waste assessment would increase to $482.16 under the city's contract with its solid waste vendor, though qualified residential homeowners would receive a one-time credit of either $364 or $64. The city also proposes a 3.5% increase in the water rate, while the sewer rate would remain unchanged.

The proposed budget also includes long-term infrastructure planning. The city says capital improvement projects over the next five years are projected to cost about $1.069 billion. The largest portion is for utility system upgrades, listed at $672.7 million. Other planned spending includes $51.1 million for Walton & One, Torino & Tradition Regional Parks and O.L. Peacock Park, $34.8 million for facilities maintenance, $24.5 million for street resurfacing and $9.9 million for sidewalk projects.

The budget brief also notes that Port St. Lucie's long-term debt has declined from more than $1.042 billion in FY 2009-10 to a projected $765 million in FY 2026-27, a reduction of 26.58% over 16 years. The proposed budget includes a net increase of seven positions in the Utility Systems Fund, bringing the city to 1,550.25 full-time equivalent positions.

City Council will review the proposed budget during a workshop July 22-23 at the Community Center, located at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

The workshop will also be televised live on the city's website, Xfinity Channel 20 and Blue Stream Fiber Channel 20.

hero.headline: Two bodies found near Sebastian appear unconnected but remain suspicious, Indian River County sheriff says
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Thursday that two bodies discovered this week near Sebastian appear unconnected but both cases remain under investigation as suspicious deaths. Sheriff Eric Flowers held a news conference Thursday morning to address the findings after autopsies were completed on both bodies.

The first body was found Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by a person fishing in the area. The deceased was identified as James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident who had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian. Thompson was last seen Sunday walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1 around 1:30 p.m. Flowers said Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues and had made a purchase of methamphetamine on July 3 before going into a manic state. The sheriff said Thompson had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County many times. According to Flowers, there was only a minor contusion on Thompson's eyebrow with no signs of violence.

The second body was found Wednesday shortly after 4 p.m. in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian and across the street from Monday's location. The heavily decomposed body was that of a 65-year-old man with a temporary address at his brother's home in Sebastian. The man had been out of jail on pretrial release after being arrested by Plantation police on a charge of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon in Broward County. Flowers said Plantation police had just obtained or was in the process of obtaining a warrant for him for absconding on his pretrial release. The man had a serious history of seizures and his brother had taken him to a hospital on Sunday. The man walked away from the hospital against medical advice around 7:30 a.m. Sunday while still wearing hospital socks, with his brother last seeing him walking north. Flowers quoted the man as saying he was not going back to the hospital.

Flowers said autopsies on both bodies showed no stab wounds or signs of violence, and nothing at this point connects the two cases. The sheriff's office is waiting on toxicology results to determine the causes of death. Flowers said the deaths could be the result of bad fentanyl or methamphetamine circulating in the area and urged drug users to seek treatment. He said the office will investigate who may have sold drugs to the men if toxicology reveals drug-related issues. Anyone with information in either case is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.
